summary_premise: The binding constraint is C1-full: it is the only condition with zero results, it is the paper's headline claim, and it is the single LLM-costly job (Harness A /hunt-experiment 5-team OBSERVE->HYPOTHESIZE->EVIDENCE->CROSS-VALIDATE->CLASSIFY per event). C2-naive re-score and C1-nohardening re-score are CHEAP (non-LLM eval helpers: c2_naive_helper.py prepare/score + compute_metrics.py + bootstrap_ci.py). C3 is already done+reproduced. Everything else (most paper prose) is data-independent and parallelizable today. So: spend the LLM budget on a SCOPED C1-full, run all cheap re-scores in parallel, and draft every non-Results paper section concurrently with data generation.

Run C1-full via /hunt-experiment (Harness A, M1-M5 + M3 framework) on the SCOPED condition set, 1 run each, full event set. Foreground, long-running. THE critical-path worker.
Re-score C2-naive on the matching new runs using c2_naive_helper.py prepare/score (no live LLM) + compute_metrics.py. Cheap, parallel with C1-full.
Re-score C1-nohardening on the matching new runs (ablation) with compute_metrics.py + compute_fpr.py. Cheap, parallel with C1-full.

Map experiment->paper: extract the actual C3 metrics + reproducibility VERDICT.json numbers, the run matrix definition, and lab/Elastic versions into a structured facts sheet the LaTeX worker consumes. No file creation, read-only synthesis.

Past tense, MDPI engproc. Runs in parallel with the experiment wave.

After data lands: convert Validation Plan -> Results (C1/C2/C3 comparison matrix tables + adversarial-resilience-by-tier story) + Discussion, wire numbers from the facts sheet, compile to PDF. Sequential after experiment wave.
Validate references.bib against authoritative sources and compile-clean the bib. Parallelizable any time.

c1_full_budget_recommendation: C1-full on 3 REPRESENTATIVE conditions, 1 run each, FULL event set: (a) control 'none' run, (b) one MID-difficulty adversarial run (e.g. per-attack-burst x encoded), (c) one HARD adversarial run (interleaved x steganographic). Rationale: the headline claim is 'governance survives adversarial log injection where naive LLM degrades' -- that needs a clean baseline + a clear difficulty gradient (easy/none -> mid -> hard), NOT all 10 runs. 3 conditions captures the resilience curve and lets C1-full be plotted against the already-scored C2/C3 on the SAME 3 runs (apples-to-apples). Running all 10 C1-full would blow the LLM/token budget on a 5-team-per-event orchestration with diminishing scientific return; the other 7 runs stay scoped as 'remaining conditions: future work / extended run' in the paper, which is honest under the no-fabrication constraint. IMPORTANT GATE: the mapping manager must verify ground_truth.jsonl is present for these 3 chosen run_ids before C1-full launches -- /hunt-experiment classifies against labels, so missing labels = wasted LLM spend. If labels exist for all 10, keep the 3-run scope anyway for budget; expand to 5 (add 2 more tiers) only if the C1-full worker reports cheap per-run cost after run (a).
wave_plan: wave 0 (sequential, 1 agent): Harness-mapping manager -- confirm ground-truth labels on new runs, map conditions to run_ids, pick the 3 C1-full target runs, lock /hunt-experiment command + output paths. Gate for everything downstream.

wave 1 (5 parallel workers): [W1] C1-full on the 3 scoped runs (critical path, foreground) | [W2] C2-naive re-score | [W3] C1-nohardening re-score | [W4] LaTeX worker drafts Methods+Setup+Related-Work+Reproducibility subsection | [W5] reference-check on references.bib. Explore facts-sheet extraction folds into W4's input.
wave 2 (sequential, 1-2 workers): assemble full C1/C2/C3 matrix from wave-1 outputs -> LaTeX worker writes Results+Discussion, builds tables/figures, splices in the wave-1 prose sections.
wave 3 (sequential, 1 worker): compile PDF, fix LaTeX/bib errors, final reference-check, deliver.
conditions: C1-full scope is CAPPED at 3 representative conditions (none + mid + hard tier), 1 run each, full event set -- not all 10 runs -- to fit one session's LLM budget. Expansion to 5 only if per-run cost proves cheap after the first run.
C2-naive and C1-nohardening MUST be re-scored on the SAME 3 run_ids that C1-full uses, so the published matrix is apples-to-apples on identical runs.
Wave 0 mapping manager MUST verify ground_truth.jsonl exists for the chosen run_ids before any C1-full LLM spend; missing labels block the launch.
Data-independent paper sections (Methods, Setup, Related Work, Reproducibility) are drafted in wave 1 IN PARALLEL with the experiment -- do not serialize prose behind data.
Any condition that cannot be run this session is scoped HONESTLY as future work in the paper; zero fabricated numbers (hard constraint).

C1-full worker runs in FOREGROUND (long-running, per CLAUDE.md no-background-agents rule) to avoid timeout/context exhaustion; if it exceeds the session, checkpoint per-run outputs to results/raw so a follow-up session resumes from the partial matrix.
key_question_for_managers: Does ground_truth.jsonl exist for the 10 new attack run_ids (2026-05-27/28), and what is the measured per-run LLM/token cost of one C1-full /hunt-experiment pass over the full event set? The 3-vs-5-vs-10 run scope decision -- and whether C1-full even fits this session -- hinges entirely on that per-run cost number, which only a single calibration run on the control 'none' condition can establish.
